rationale: Spent the remaining budget on one bounded source check outside the feature audited so far: the network transport's heartbeat fast path, which invokes the Raft heartbeat handler from the transport goroutine rather than the main loop. The guard is conservative - a request is treated as a heartbeat only when it has a term, a leader address, zero previous-log index and term, no entries and a zero leader commit index - and the handler itself only handles AppendEntries and returns early when the node is shut down, so the fast path cannot append entries or apply committed entries off the main loop. I recorded that as a sourced negative rather than a suspicion, and no conclusion in the run changes.

knowledge.statement: The network transport routes an AppendEntries request to the heartbeat handler in its own goroutine only when the decoded request has a non-zero term, a leader address, zero PrevLogEntry and PrevLogTerm, no entries and a zero LeaderCommitIndex; every other AppendEntries request is dispatched to the Raft main loop. The handler accepts only AppendEntries commands and returns immediately when the node is shutting down, so the off-main-loop path cannot append entries or apply committed entries for the follower.
knowledge.conditions: NetworkTransport RPC decoding and dispatch; the equivalent InmemTransport does not implement the fast path (its SetHeartbeatHandler is a no-op), so this applies to the network transport only.
